stories.title: Armed police begin patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach shooting
stories.summary: Heavily‑armed officers from New South Wales’ Armed Response Command have started patrolling Sydney’s streets and tourist precincts with long‑arm rifles. The deployment follows the December mass shooting at Bondi Beach that killed fifteen people, including a ten‑year‑old girl. Police say the units will also patrol major events such as sports matches and places of worship to deter and respond quickly to serious threats.
stories.why: It represents a notable escalation in public‑security tactics after Australia’s deadliest mass shooting in decades.

stories.title: Judge lets NAACP lawsuit over xAI data‑center emissions proceed
stories.summary: A federal judge denied xAI’s motion to dismiss an NAACP‑led suit that alleges the company installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines at its Colossus data center outside Memphis without the required pre‑construction or operating air permits, in violation of the Clean Air Act. The Southern Environmental Law Center, representing the NAACP, argued the turbines are not “mobile sources” under Mississippi law, and Judge Debra M. Brown affirmed the plaintiffs have statutory standing and that the citizen‑suit claim is constitutional.
stories.why: The decision lets the lawsuit continue, which could require xAI to obtain permits and address alleged air‑pollution violations.
stories.previousTitle: Judge denies xAI motion to dismiss NAACP lawsuit over data‑center emissions
stories.previousSummary: A federal judge rejected xAI’s motion to dismiss a lawsuit brought by the NAACP and the Southern Environmental Law Center that alleges the SpaceX‑owned AI firm operated at least 35 combustion turbines at its Colossus data center outside Memphis without the required pre‑construction or operating air permits, violating the Clean Air Act. The decision affirmed the plaintiffs’ statutory standing and held that the turbines are not “mobile sources,” so the case will continue.
